samples.summary: The checkout-keying of the round store is only tested as a pure function; nothing tests that `cmdReview` actually passes the checkout root to `reviewBase`
samples.evidence: `reviewBase(branch, repo)` gets a direct unit test (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:555-573) with hand-supplied repo strings, but every CLI-level `review` test in the file passes `--out` (lines 369, 452, 588, 606, 801, 849, 980, 1037, 1135, 1174), and `--out` short-circuits the default: `const requested = args.out ? path.resolve(args.out) : reviewBase(branch, repoRoot)` (spec-to-pr.mjs:993). So the new wiring added by this delta — `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, the `process.cwd()` fallback, the `realpathSync` resolve (spec-to-pr.mjs:984-990), and passing that value as the second argument — is never executed in a way that can fail a test. If the second argument were dropped, or the branch were passed twice, or the cwd were used instead of the toplevel, every test here would still be green while two checkouts on `main` again shared a store (the cross-repo verdict-into-prompt leak the change exists to close). A dry run prints the resolved round dir (spec-to-pr.mjs:1127), so two staged fixture checkouts on the same branch name could be run without `--out` and their printed paths compared — this file's own stated ethos is that 'wiring is exactly where this file's defects have lived'.

finding.summary: The blocking-verdict report path (`blockingFindingsIn` → `renderBlockingFindings` → exit 1) is untested: no test drives a panel.json with a blocking lens
finding.evidence: `blockingFindingsIn` (spec-to-pr.mjs:873) is a new, non-exported function that reads each failing lens's `verdict.json` from the round directory and feeds `carryForwardFindings` into `renderBlockingFindings` (:1112), then exits 1 (:1119). It is reachable only through the CLI, and the only CLI test that gets past the panel spawn uses a recorder stub that writes `[{ id: "docs", conclusion: "success" }]` (`writeRecorderPanel`, spec-to-pr.test.mjs:~838), so the blocking branch never runs. `renderBlockingFindings` is unit-tested on hand-built `[{lens, findings}]` fixtures (:180, :197) — which is exactly the both-ends-tested-but-not-the-join pattern the diff's own comments say this change exists to fix (see the comment at spec-to-pr.mjs:~860 about the wiring being where defects live). Nothing asserts that a blocking lens's verdict on disk actually produces a non-zero exit, the per-finding lines, or the "re-run for round N+1" guidance; a regression there turns a blocking local review into output a developer reads as clean.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists. scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.test.mjs:1092 ("review: a blocking verdict is reported with its findings and exits 1") spawns the real CLI (`node spec-to-pr.mjs review --out base`, :1135) against a purpose-built stub panel (:1100-1129, NOT writeRecorderPanel) that writes docs/verdict.json with a major finding, a crash-shaped security/verdict.json, and a panel.json containing two failing lenses plus a success and an applicable:false failure. It asserts exit status 1 (:1149, the process.exit(1) at spec-to-pr.mjs:1210), the "2 blocking lens verdict(s): docs, security" line (:1151, exercising the applicability filter at spec-to-pr.mjs:1199), the per-finding line "[major] docs — added.ts:3" plus summary and key (:1153-1155), the "no finding recorded" branch (:1158), and the "re-run for round 2" guidance (:1160, from spec-to-pr.mjs:1206). This drives blockingFindingsIn -> carryForwardFindings -> renderBlockingFindings -> exit 1 from a panel.json on disk, i.e. exactly the join the finding says is untested. The finding's premises are also factually wrong: blockingFindingsIn is exported (spec-to-pr.mjs:953, imported at test :33) and directly unit-tested on a real round directory at test :1063-1090.
